papers.title: State as Computation
papers.current_ceiling: The width-conditioned bounded result remains; the ten-responsibility study is negative and the tie-robust successor returned T3_TIE_AMBIGUOUS_VERDICT_CHANGING.
post_matrix_updates: The live manuscript/ledger still needs to absorb the ten-responsibility negative and retire older positive-assuming CI language.
load_bearing_adverse: LINEAR reaches 3/10 and RBF/KNN 5/10 against a frozen at-least-8/10 gate.
The tie-robust phase verdict is ambiguous and confirms withdrawal rather than rescue.
V1 executable bytes are absent; only a post-outcome-modified variant survives in quarantine.
papers.strongest_remaining_gap: A new question must treat the phase boundary as set-valued under ties and test responsibility-conditioned placement of computation in real procedural systems with end-to-end resource accounting.
papers.decisive_question: Can a set-valued responsibility-conditioned policy choose where to compute state—upfront, on demand or not at all—so that it improves verified utility under matched resources across real procedural domains without laundering tied optima?
papers.maximum_claim_if_supported: Computational placement is governed by downstream responsibility and admits a robust set-valued phase law under ties, rather than one universal scalar boundary.
papers.hypothesis_or_theorem: A policy trained only on design tasks should predict a set of admissible placements whose verified regret is near-optimal and whose tie coverage is calibrated across independent domains.
papers.population_or_universe: Prospectively frozen tasks from a software/procedural domain and a paper-disjoint E2 or E12 family, each with objective downstream responsibilities and placement choices.
design: Update the bounded manuscript with the negative and ambiguity before successor design.
Define placement choices and responsibilities with native downstream verifiers.
Represent ties as admissible sets, not forced single labels.
Match preprocessing, memory, inference and tool resources across placements.
Hold out projects/task families and test calibrated set coverage.
primary_endpoints: Full resource vector and unsafe decision rate.
negative_controls: Task where no computation is optimal.
analysis_plan: No single-label accuracy metric may penalize a correctly retained tie.
Preprocessing/compiler work remains in the resource ledger.
papers.power_or_exhaustion_rule: Power at the project/task-family level and include a prospectively fixed minimum number of strict optima and genuine ties in each domain.
papers.success_gate: The frozen policy covers true optimal placements, achieves lower verified regret than fixed-placement baselines and retains calibrated optionality across domains under full accounting.
papers.refutation_gate: Poor tie coverage, hidden preprocessing or no cross-domain regret gain preserves only the bounded/negative result.
papers.cannot_check_gate: CANNOT_CHECK if V1 lineage is used, responsibilities/placements change after outcomes or any resource coordinate is missing.
papers.authority_required: Native downstream verifiers and an independent resource/placement evaluator; no quarantined post-outcome variant may supply authority.

active_lane.collision_rule: Do not revive the V1 ladder or use quarantined modified bytes as faithful replay.

immediate_safe_actions: Integrate LINEAR 3/10, RBF/KNN 5/10 and T3 ambiguity into the live ledger/manuscript.
Define set-valued placement and tie metrics.
Select paper-disjoint procedural domains and native responsibilities.
forbidden_actions: Do not force ties into one positive phase label.
Do not treat the quarantined post-outcome variant as V1 evidence.
papers.journal_bar: A top-tier learning/systems paper needs set-valued tie handling, real procedural responsibilities, end-to-end resource accounting, donor-complete comparators and external transfer.
papers.sibling_boundary: Owns where computation is placed; whether state is valuable belongs to ORION-08 and online next-resource choice to ORION-22.
